text: Every research paper makes claims. Numbers, comparisons, conclusions.
Checking whether the paper's own tables and results actually support them is slow, manual work.
ClaimCheck AI makes that check systematic. Because research claims deserve evidence.
Drop in a PDF. This one is a synthetic test paper, with problems planted on purpose.
ClaimCheck reads the layout, maps the sections and tables, and picks out the sentences that make checkable claims.
Nine claims audited. Each one is tied to evidence in the same document, or flagged when that evidence is missing.
It separates missing evidence, numbers that disagree between sections, and claims that reach beyond the experiments.
Every finding shows its classification, its confidence, and exactly where the claim appears.
This results paragraph matches Table 2 exactly, so it is marked supported.
But the abstract reports ninety-eight point two percent accuracy, while Table 2 reports ninety-four point one for the same model. ClaimCheck shows both values, the gap, and the exact table row.
One click shows that evidence in the extracted text, on page two.
Or ask by voice. In this illustration, Wispr Flow dictates the question into the input field.
The answer comes only from the audit record: Table 2, page two, flagged for review, not proof of an error.
A flag is not proof that the science is wrong. The reviewer decides, and that decision stays separate from the engine's label.
Export the full report, with every claim, quote, page, and check.
ClaimCheck AI. Evidence first. Uncertainty stated. Nothing invented.
